newsitem.title: UK: LME copper directionless, zinc hits fresh peak.
newsitem.headline: LME copper directionless, zinc hits fresh peak.

text.p: LME copper prices thrashed around on Thursday, ending nearly back where they started after a morning foray down towards key support.
"Copper seems unable to break out of its range. It's not able to find any direction," said analyst Helen Williamson at broker Brandeis.
Three months copper ended the day only $1 firmer at $2,339 per tonne after touching a low of $2,312, the point where it broke to the upside about a month ago.
Traders said Chinese buying propped up prices at the day's lows.
Volumes have been lacklustre, except at the top and bottom of the range, one senior dealer said.
Chartists note that Thursday's low coincides with the 30-day moving average and raises the prospect that copper may now oscillate in a price band capped by the 10-day average on the upside at $2,373.
The premium of cash over three month metal widened slightly to $52/$58 from about $46 on Wednesday.
Preliminary estimates on LME copper data for Friday hover around a 3,000 tonne draw.
Metal has been moving into Comex warehouses since the New York market went into a premium on February 25, Williamson said. The premium current stood at 5 cents/lb or $130 per tonne, she added.
Zinc shook off copper's confusing moves, notching up a fresh 4-1/2 year peak of $1,287 on speculative buying, traders said.
It ended the day $5 higher at $1,280.
The options market has seen good buying interest in both zinc calls and puts, options dealers said. Chinese producers were taking insurance by buying $1,200 puts, one said.
The market may press on towards the $1,300 mark if inventory data show a draw, Williamson said. "We might see $1,300 before people come in and sell," she said.
Aluminium kept to a narrow range, finishing $8 weaker at $1,658.
The market has lost energy and tests of support at $1,650 and $1,630 may be on the cards, Williamson said.
Lead, finding it difficult to revisit the $700 mark, finished the day unchanged at $693 while tin added $20 to $6,050.
Nickel kept to its recent range, closing $10 weaker at $8,060.
